A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Data Laundering study. Their complete main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and can be matched reliably despite revisions and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original BERT/GPT-2 experiments, loss and data-size ablations, iterative distillation results, and artificial-data experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds LLaMA teacher/student results and semantic and lexical comparisons of the training datasets with GPQA.

M1.justification: The teacher-contamination, intermediate-data distillation, and benchmark-evaluation procedure remains unchanged, including the hard/soft-label mixture and MSE/KLD options. LLaMA models are additional experimental configurations; deleting component-loss formulas does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use GPQA Diamond and MMLU-Redux for benchmark evaluation and MedMCQA and RACE for distillation. The artificial-data scenarios already appear in v1 Appendix C. New model configurations and comparisons of existing datasets do not expand dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same external baselines and ordinary BERT/GPT-2 comparisons. Added LLaMA rows represent contaminated teachers and students using the proposed procedure. MiniLLM, DistiLLM, and SinKD are newly discussed but are not evaluated as competing methods.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 substantially expands tested model configurations with LLaMA3.2-1B/3B students and LLaMA3.2-3B/LLaMA3.1-8B teachers. The new similarity analysis uses Sentence-BERT cosine scores, a 0.5 threshold, and vocabulary overlap. Table 1 also corrects ordinary BERT/GPT-2 training labels to MedMCQA/RACE, consistent with v1's prose; this does not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 5.1 adds semantic and lexical similarity analysis to investigate the previously hypothesized advantage of MedMCQA's domain alignment with GPQA. Existing loss/alpha, iterative-distillation, data-size, and artificial-data analyses remain, with unchanged supporting plots and appendix results.

E5.justification: v1 provides point estimates and seed 42 in Table 5. v2 introduces three-run averaging and ± reporting for most Table 1 distillation results, except configurations using the 8B teacher, and identifies other results as single-run. This substantially changes uncertainty reporting, although the ± statistic and additional seeds are unspecified; an actual increase in runs cannot be established.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces existing distillation point estimates with revised averages and adds LLaMA results. For example, BERT-2/KD(1) on MedMCQA changes from 74.75/62.83 to 73.94/62.31, while BERT-2/KD(2) on RACE changes from 60.10/47.10 to 46.44/38.49. These are revised reported results, not established same-setting gains or losses. New similarity findings include 47 versus 2 semantic matches and 162 versus 15 lexical matches. Appendix A results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 retains the combined-loss equation but removes explicit cross-entropy, MSE, and KLD formulas and the temperature, logit, and softmax definitions. This is a limited reduction in mathematical specification. Neither version presents theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, numbered contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: distillation can intentionally or unintentionally transfer benchmark contamination, a small BERT model can approach 75% GPQA accuracy, and evaluation needs stronger safeguards. Added experiments support the existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v2 extends the model-size interpretation to LLaMA, supports domain alignment with similarity evidence, and recommends teachers with documented training data. It adds encoded-test-data future work. The limitations remove model-size and noise/domain-shift/adversarial caveats and soften the warning that small datasets may exaggerate laundering effects.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly identifies A100 hardware for LLaMA training and an RTX 4090 for BERT/GPT-2. Section 4.1 specifies sources for external baseline scores. The code link and Table 5 hyperparameter values remain unchanged; corresponding LLaMA hyperparameters are not added.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 shifts toward logit-based distillation, adding MiniLLM, DistiLLM, and SinKD while removing the SimPO-related discussion. Section 5.5 adds LLM360 as a transparency example. Updated publication metadata and consolidation of duplicate MMLU references do not represent new research coverage.

P1.justification: v2 edits the abstract and methodological explanations, clarifies iterative teacher/student succession, adds descriptive results subheadings, shortens several discussions, and rewrites the limitations. The overall section sequence and Appendices A–C remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 expands with LLaMA rows, ± formatting, clearer dataset labels, and a revised caption. Table 5 groups its batch-size headings. Figure 3 moves between columns and surrounding text reflows, but all five figures retain the same artwork and plotted results.

improvement.justification: Repeated-run reporting strengthens the main empirical results, and the new similarity analysis provides evidence for v1's domain-alignment hypothesis. LLaMA experiments and hardware disclosures also add useful support. These gains are limited by undefined ± statistics, missing LLaMA hyperparameters and clean controls, and removal of explicit loss formulas and real-world generalization caveats. Overall, the empirical support improves modestly.
